page.layout: One column of text on a single printed page. Each entry is a bare number, then an italic keyword with a bracket, then a gloss and a scripture reference. A vertical side title runs down the right margin. Running head at top left, page number at top right.

main_text.p: Luxus] Pro voluptate ducunt quotidianas delicias. 2. Pet. 2,13.
Fraudes] Labes ac maculæ, quæ fraudibus se oblectant. 2. Pet. 2,13.
Turpitudo] Oculos habentes plenos adulterii, & qui à peccando cessare nesciant. 2. Pet. 2,14.
Artes perpetuæ] Inscantes[?] animas instabiles. 2. Pet. 2,14.
Deploratus amor habendi] Cor habentes ad avaritiam excitatum. 2. Pet. 2,14.
Impia maledicentia] Execrandi homines, qui relicta recta via aberrarunt, secuti viam Balaami filii Bosor, qui mercedem iniquitatis amavit. 2. Pet. 2,15.IESVITARVM.
Vanitas] Isti sunt fontes aqua carentes, nebulæ à turbine exagitatæ &c. 2. Pet. 2,17.
Ambitio noxia] Prætumidam vanitatem loquendo per carnis cupiditates lascivas eos inescant, qui verè effugerant eos qui in errore versantur. 2. Pet. 2,18.
Falsa iactantia] Libertatem pollicentur, quæ ipsi servi sint corruptionis. 2. Pet. 2,19.

page.notes: The leading mark before "Artes perpetuæ" and "Ambitio noxia" is an ornamental letter or sign that I could not identify; I have omitted it. "Inscantes" is doubtful: the printed letters are unclear and may be a misprint. The side title IESVITARVM. is set vertically in the right margin and is recorded as a note. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout, including "Bosor", read from the long-s form. Hyphenated line breaks are joined: "adulterii", "nebulæ", "inescant". Printed spelling, including "verè" and "quæ", is kept as printed.
